title: Petroleum Engineer Salary: Award Rates, Hourly Conversion, and Annual Pay Guide
description: Understand the petroleum engineer salary using award rates from Fair Work, hourly-to-annual conversion for 38-hour weeks, plus tax and super estimates for 2026–27.
salarySummary: A petroleum engineer covered by the Hydrocarbons Industry Award earns at least $31.42 per hour (Level 4) for a 38-hour week, equating to about $62,100 annually before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a petroleum engineer under the award?
faqs.a: Under the Hydrocarbons Industry (Upstream) Award 2020, a petroleum engineer is typically classified at Level 4 (Advanced) or Level 5 (Advanced Specialist). From 1 July 2026, the minimum hourly rate for Level 4 is $31.42 and for Level 5 is $33.47. These rates include the industry allowance and apply to full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, bringing the casual rate to $39.28 per hour for Level 4.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly petroleum engineer rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, a Level 4 petroleum engineer at $31.42 per hour earns $31.42 × 38 × 52 = $62,085.92 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to calculate your own figures.

faqs.q: Does the petroleum engineer salary include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your base salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a petroleum engineer earning $62,100 per year, the employer would contribute an additional $7,452 in super. This is not included in the hourly or annual salary figures shown in award rates or pay guides.

bodyMarkdown:
## Petroleum Engineer Salary: Award Rates and Annual Pay

When researching a **petroleum engineer salary**, it helps to start with the minimum standards set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. The Hydrocarbons Industry (Upstream) Award 2020 covers many petroleum engineers working in oil and gas extraction. This award provides minimum hourly rates, penalty loadings, and conditions. However, many petroleum engineers are employed under enterprise agreements or individual contracts that pay above the award. Understanding the award floor gives you a baseline for negotiations or budget planning.

### Hourly to Annual Conversion for a 38-Hour Week

Most full-time petroleum engineers work an average of 38 ordinary hours per week, as defined by the award. To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a 38-hour week, that’s hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, a petroleum engineer at the award’s Level 4 (Advanced) rate of $31.42 per hour earns:

$31.42 × 38 × 52 = $62,085.92 per year.

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply the weekly amount by 2. Using the same rate, the weekly pay is $1,193.96 (38 × $31.42), so the fortnightly gross is $2,387.92. This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a more personalised estimate, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool.

### Award Rates vs Market Rates

The award rates for petroleum engineers are set out in the Hydrocarbons Industry Award pay guide. Key adult minimum rates from 1 July 2026 include:

- Level 4 (Advanced): $31.42 per hour, $1,193.90 per week
- Level 5 (Advanced Specialist): $33.47 per hour, $1,271.80 per week
- Level 6 (Dual Trade): $35.11 per hour, $1,334.10 per week

These rates already include the all-purpose industry allowance of $66.70 per week. Compare these to the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week) and the Australian Bureau of Statistics’ Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees of $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). The ABS figure suggests many petroleum engineers earn well above the award, reflecting specialised skills and industry demand.

Casual petroleum engineers receive a 25% loading on top of the ordinary hourly rate. For Level 4, the casual rate is $39.28 per hour ($31.42 × 1.25). This loading compensates for lost entitlements like annual leave and sick pay. If you are a casual, do not enter a rate that already includes the loading into our calculator; instead, use the base rate and check the casual loading box.

### Tax and Superannuation Considerations

Your annual petroleum engineer salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not confirmed). For a petroleum engineer earning $62,100, the tax would be approximately $9,967 plus Medicare of $1,242, leaving around $50,891 after tax. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed breakdown.

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $62,100 salary, the employer contributes an extra $7,452 per year. This is not deducted from your pay; it goes into your super fund. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2. For a petroleum engineer on the Level 4 award rate, the fortnightly gross is $2,387.92. After tax and Medicare, the net fortnightly amount would be roughly $1,957. This can help with budgeting for rent, bills, and savings. Remember that award rates are minimums; many petroleum engineers earn significantly more, especially those with experience or working in remote locations.

For a complete picture of your potential earnings, refer to our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). These resources include penalty rates, allowances, and overtime provisions that may apply to your specific role. Always check your employment contract or enterprise agreement for the exact terms.
